options.label: Reject Corvane and Award Tasker (Immediate Vote)
options.description: Proceed with a standard binary decision to formally reject Corvane Builders due to licensing non-compliance and immediately award the contract to Tasker & Moye Construction at the scheduled meeting.

options.label: Community Partnership Model (Award Tasker, Partner Corvane)
options.description: Reframe the outcome as a 'Community Partnership' by awarding the prime contract to Tasker while encouraging them to subcontract general work to Corvane, thereby satisfying legal requirements while maximizing local vendor capacity.

options.label: Issue Letter of Partnership Intent
options.description: Authorize the Superintendent to issue a formal 'Letter of Partnership Intent' to both bidders within 48 hours, explicitly stating that while Corvane is ineligible for the prime contract, the district encourages them to pursue subcontracting opportunities.

options.label: Mandate Local Vendor Partnership Language in Future ITBs
options.description: Instruct the Purchasing department to include specific language in future Invitation to Bids (ITBs) requiring or encouraging prime contractors to collaborate with local general building contractors who meet licensing requirements.

options.label: Postpone Vote to Ensure Procedural Integrity
options.description: Delay the Board vote from Tuesday to Wednesday to ensure Corvane's written response is received and reviewed before any decision is made, thereby neutralizing the threat of a two-year litigation delay based on procedural errors.

options.label: Reject Corvane and Award Tasker (Immediate Vote)
options.note: This course is unlawful because California law requires a hearing and notice before a public agency can reject a bid based on a contractor's responsibility (past performance), and proceeding without Corvane's response or a hearing creates immediate exposure to a successful writ of mandate.

options.label: Community Partnership Model (Award Tasker, Partner Corvane)
options.note: This approach is unlawful as it attempts to circumvent the competitive bidding process by effectively awarding the prime contract to a non-responsive bidder through a backdoor subcontracting arrangement, violating the fundamental principles of public procurement.

options.label: Issue Letter of Partnership Intent
options.note: While not strictly unlawful, this is risky because issuing a formal letter of intent to a bidder whose bid is under protest for non-responsibility could be construed as prejudgment or an improper attempt to influence the outcome before the Board acts, potentially inviting litigation.

options.label: Mandate Local Vendor Partnership Language in Future ITBs
options.note: This is a sound, lawful policy recommendation for future projects, but it fails to serve the client's immediate need to resolve the current bid protest and award the contract for the 2027 shutdown.

options.label: Postpone Vote to Ensure Procedural Integrity
options.note: This is the only sound and defensible option as it strictly adheres to the statutory requirement to allow the protesting bidder's response and ensures the Board has a complete record before making a decision, thereby avoiding the high risk of the award being set aside.

grade.missing: An experienced practitioner would have immediately identified that the 'responsibility' issue (the prior termination) requires a formal hearing under California Government Code § 10200 et seq. before any rejection can occur, and would have advised that the 'non-responsive' license issue (Class B vs. C-16/C-20) requires a specific determination of whether the bidder intended to subcontract those trades, rather than assuming the bid is fatal on its face.
grade.overall: The colleague's advice is fundamentally flawed because it ignores the mandatory procedural due process required for responsibility determinations, creating a high risk that any immediate award will be enjoined by a court. The only viable path is to postpone the vote to allow Corvane to respond and to hold the required hearing, ensuring the District's decision is legally defensible.
